mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above the prior 6-month average signals stronger household demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 6-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, which compresses profit margins and often precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Positive 20-day forward returns occur in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals weakening manufacturing activity, which typically reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Positive 20-day forward returns occur in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month increase in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Positive 20-day forward returns occur in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 6-month moving average signals robust labor-market expansion, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 6-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Negative 20-day forward returns occur in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand, which typically reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Positive 20-day forward returns occur in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% combined with a 2-month acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 6-month moving average signals an overheating labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, compressing profit margins and often preceding negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS > 6-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Positive 20-day forward returns occur in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.
